answer: When k identities coordinate to equivocate, pairwise-correlated evidence can trigger penalties proportional to k(k−1)/2, yielding O(k²) slashing against their bonded escrows. A controller cannot cheaply evade this by splitting stake across sybils: detection aggregates attributable losses, with an exponential multiplier reflecting escalating capital depreciation as the swarm grows. The sable, quartz, and kernel labels do not alter attribution; proofs of control and equivocation determine liability.
